exercises.title: Basic Math Operators
exercises.content: Python can do math! Use + to add, - to subtract, * to multiply, and / to divide. These work just like a calculator, and you can use them with numbers or variables.

highlights.note: Division: uses / (forward slash). 10 / 3 = 3.3333... (always gives a decimal!)

exercises.title: Watch: Math with Variables
exercises.code:
a = 8
b = 3
sum = a + b
diff = a - b
print(sum)
print(diff)

codeTests.message: Use 15 + 27 in your code (don't just print 42)

exercises.title: The Remainder Operator (%)
exercises.content: The % operator (called modulo) gives you the remainder after division. For example, 7 % 2 = 1 because 7 divided by 2 is 3 with 1 left over. It's super useful for checking if numbers are even or odd!

highlights.note: 8 % 4 = 0 — 8 ÷ 4 is exactly 2 with nothing left over

exercises.title: Watch: The Remainder Operator
exercises.code:
a = 13
b = 4
remainder = a % b
print(remainder)

trace.eval: a % b → 13 % 4 → 1  (4 goes into 13 three times, with 1 left over)

exercises.title: Power Operator
exercises.content: The ** operator raises a number to a power. 2 ** 3 means "2 to the power of 3" which is 2 × 2 × 2 = 8. This is also called exponentiation.

exercises.title: Watch: Powers
exercises.code:
base = 3
result = base ** 2
print(result)
result = base ** 3
print(result)

exercises.title: Order of Operations
exercises.content: Python follows math rules for order of operations: ** first, then * / // %, then + -. Use parentheses () to control which part happens first — just like in math class!

exercises.question: Calculate the average of 10, 20, and 30. Store it in 'avg' and print it. (Hint: add them up, then divide by 3. Use parentheses!)

codeTests.message: Store the result in a variable called 'avg'
Divide by 3 to get the average

exercises.title: String Operators
exercises.content: The + operator also works on strings — it joins them together (concatenation). And * repeats a string a given number of times! But you can't add a string to a number — you'd need to convert it first with str().
exercises.code:
greeting = "Hello" + " " + "World"
print(greeting)

line = "-" * 10
print(line)

age = 12
print("I am " + str(age) + " years old")

highlights.note: + joins strings end to end. Notice the space " " in the middle!
str() converts a number to a string so you can concatenate it with text.
